# Features and why to use them

[Example documentation](README.md)

Each row is a capability the example shows, why a developer would use it, and where to learn how.

**Table 1 — Features**

| Capability | Why use it | Framework features | Guide | Run book |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Explore the examples | One place to confirm every example endpoint is alive and to jump to the API and event references, before you start coding against them. | OoBDev.Example.WebApi; OoBDev.AspNetCore.Mvc (OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents) | [guide](user-guide/explore-the-examples.md) | [run book](runbooks/explore-the-examples.md) |
| Chat with a local model | Talk to a model that runs on your machine with no API key and no data leaving it, through the same `IMessageCompletion` interface you would use for a cloud model. | OoBDev.AI.Abstractions (`IMessageCompletion`, `IStreamedCompletion`); OoBDev.Ollama | [guide](user-guide/chat-with-a-local-model.md) | [run book](runbooks/chat-with-a-local-model.md) |
| Hold a conversation with Ollama | Keep context between questions by passing the previous exchange, so follow-ups are understood. | OoBDev.AI.Abstractions (`CompletionRequest.Context`); OoBDev.Ollama | [guide](user-guide/hold-a-conversation.md) | [run book](runbooks/hold-a-conversation.md) |
| Compare two texts with embeddings | Turn text into vectors and measure similarity in process, the basis of semantic search, deduplication and clustering without a remote service. | OoBDev.Onnx.SentenceEmbeddings; OoBDev.AI.Abstractions (`IEmbeddingProvider`) | [guide](user-guide/compare-two-texts.md) | [run book](runbooks/compare-two-texts.md) |
| Ask a question about your own text | Ground answers in your own text (retrieval augmented generation) so the model answers from your passages instead of guessing. | OoBDev.Onnx.SentenceEmbeddings; OoBDev.Ollama; OoBDev.AI.Abstractions | [guide](user-guide/ask-your-own-documents.md) | [run book](runbooks/ask-your-own-documents.md) |
| Check the running service | See the environment, runtime and effective configuration of a running API without shell access; secrets are masked. | OoBDev.AspNetCore.Mvc; Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration | [guide](user-guide/check-the-running-service.md) | [run book](runbooks/check-the-running-service.md) |
| Cache a value | Keep expensive results close by behind one interface; switch between in-memory and Redis by configuration, not code. | OoBDev.Caching (`ICachingProvider`); OoBDev.Microsoft.Caching; OoBDev.Redis.Caching | [guide](user-guide/cache-a-value.md) | [run book](runbooks/cache-a-value.md) |
| Hash, sign and compare | Pick the algorithm by key from configuration instead of hard-coding it; the default hash is SHA-512, and signing and vector math are one call each. | OoBDev.System (`IHash`, `IHMACCalculator`); OoBDev.System.Abstractions (`VectorMath`) | [guide](user-guide/use-the-toolbox.md) | [run book](runbooks/use-the-toolbox.md) |
| Render a text template | Generate emails, pages and documents from files named after template, target type and engine, so content changes without code changes. | OoBDev.Text.Templating | [guide](user-guide/render-a-template.md) | [run book](runbooks/render-a-template.md) |
| Send an email through a channel | Send mail through the communications abstraction, so channels can change without touching callers. | OoBDev.Communications; OoBDev.MailKit | [guide](user-guide/send-an-email.md) | [run book](runbooks/send-an-email.md) |
| Put a message on a queue | Hand work to a queue through one interface so RabbitMQ, Service Bus, Storage queues or SQS can be swapped by configuration. | OoBDev.MessageQueue; OoBDev.AsyncApi | [guide](user-guide/queue-a-message.md) | [run book](runbooks/queue-a-message.md) |
| Convert and store a document | Convert and store documents (text, HTML, PDF, markdown) behind one service, so callers never depend on a converter library. | OoBDev.Documents | [guide](user-guide/convert-a-document.md) | [run book](runbooks/convert-a-document.md) |
| Sign in with Keycloak | Authenticate with OpenID Connect and PKCE so the SPA and API handle only tokens, never passwords. | OoBDev.Identity; OoBDev.AspNetCore.JwtAuthentication; Keycloak (authorization code with PKCE) | [guide](user-guide/sign-in.md) | [run book](runbooks/sign-in.md) |
| See the claims on your token | Inspect the claims the API sees on your token, the quickest way to debug roles and rights. | OoBDev.Identity; Keycloak (OIDC, JWT bearer) | [guide](user-guide/see-who-you-are.md) | [run book](runbooks/see-who-you-are.md) |
